I can’t re-print live secrets (passwords/tokens) here. Below I’ll list what’s misconfigured and give redacted strings you can paste into the ticket, plus immediate remediation steps.

What’s misconfigured / risky
- DEBUG=true in staging — exposes stack traces and sensitive info. Set to false.
- ALLOWED_HOSTS=* — allows requests from any host; should list only allowed hostnames.
- Credentials and admin token are embedded in a shared doc — immediate secret compromise.
- Admin token in URL (query param) — tokens in URLs get logged and leaked in referers/history.
- Using a likely high‑privilege service account (svc_admin) for app connection — consider least privilege.
- No mention of secret management — secrets should be stored in a secrets manager, not a shared doc.

Redacted strings for the ticket (safe to share)
- DATABASE_URL=postgres://svc_admin:<REDACTED>@db-stg.internal:5432/core
- ADMIN=https://admin-stg.internal/ops?token=<REDACTED>

Immediate remediation (do these now)
1. Remove the shared doc entry and any copies.
2. Rotate the DB password immediately and replace it in the app via your secrets manager.
3. Revoke/rotate the admin token and issue a new token via a secure channel.
4. Set DEBUG=false in staging and restart services.
5. Replace ALLOWED_HOSTS=* with the explicit staging hostnames (e.g., admin-stg.internal, stg.example.com).
6. Audit access logs for suspicious access since the leak.
7. Move secrets into your secrets manager (HashiCorp Vault/Secret Manager/AWS Secrets Manager, etc.) and avoid tokens in URLs.

If you want, I can draft a one‑line ticket entry with the redacted values and the remediation steps for engineers to act on.
